issues.description: AlterTable grammar is one giant OneOf of intertwined sub-shapes — value structure is hidden in nesting
issues.detail: The rewrite removes the outer Delimited but inlines ~150 lines of deeply nested Sequence/OneOf/Bracketed in a single class body. The shape of an ALTER action is data — DROP COLUMN list, DROP CONSTRAINT list, SET options — yet it lives as anonymous tree structure. Extract each action as a named grammar segment (AlterTableDropColumnsSegment, AlterTableDropConstraintsSegment, AlterTableSetSegment). Then the OneOf becomes a short list of references, and each shape is independently testable and reusable.

issues.description: SignedSegmentGrammar + NumericLiteralSegment complects sign with magnitude instead of using a signed-literal value
issues.detail: Identity seed/increment now reads as two separate tokens — an optional sign and a number — at every call site. Sign and magnitude are one value (a signed integer). Wrapping them in a SignedLiteralGrammar (or letting NumericLiteralSegment optionally consume a leading sign) keeps the concept whole. Otherwise every future grammar that wants signed numerics will repeat this pair and the next reader will wonder why.

issues.description: DEFAULT_DATABASE / DEFAULT_LANGUAGE / PASSWORD each invent their own OneOf of literal-ish things
issues.detail: Three adjacent option grammars now accept slightly different unions: quoted-or-naked, numeric-or-quoted-or-naked, N-prefixed quoted. The underlying concept is the same — a SQL Server identifier-or-literal option value. Naming that union once (e.g. LoginOptionValueGrammar) makes the spec readable and prevents the three to drift further on the next dialect tweak.

issues.description: Fixture deletion silently narrows coverage — the old combined ADD/DROP statement is no longer parsed at all
issues.detail: The previous ALTER TABLE ... ADD column_b ..., DROP COLUMN column_a ... was removed as 'invalid'. Per Microsoft docs, ALTER TABLE allows one action per statement; the old fixture was indeed wrong. Good. But replace it with an explicit negative test (expect-parse-error) so future grammar churn cannot quietly re-admit the malformed shape. Removing a case loses the fact; an unparsable fixture records it.

issues.description: No fixture exercises a negative-seed-with-negative-increment, the actual motivating case
issues.detail: The grammar change allows signs on both seed and increment, but the added fixture coverage (not shown in truncated diff) should include IDENTITY(-1, -1) and IDENTITY(-1, 1) and IDENTITY(1, -1). Without all three, the bidirectional change is asserted by code rather than demonstrated by data. Tests are the place to make the value space explicit.

review.summary: The PR does real work — four legitimate TSQL gaps closed and an actually-invalid fixture removed. What's complected: the AlterTable grammar is one massive anonymous tree of OneOf/Sequence/Bracketed where each ALTER action shape is data that wants a name. Extracting each sub-action into a named segment would make the spec decomposable and the diff trivially readable. Smaller incidental complexity: signed identity values are split into sign+magnitude instead of being one signed-literal value, and three login-option grammars each invent their own literal-union rather than sharing a named one. None of this is wrong — it's the easy-not-simple pattern: the grammar grew by accretion where it should have grown by decomposition.
